# Chromium 158 / Firefox 160 native QPACK vectors

These eight vectors come from actual ordinary-browser interface captures,
independently authenticated and reconstructed before export. Each contains
**twelve** requests: an ordinary HTTP/3 discovery warm request and eleven
application requests. Historical sibling fixtures keep their eleven requests
and actual Chromium 156 / Firefox 159 provenance.

The matching Surf source fixture URL, its SHA-256 and the actual interface pcap
SHA-256 are embedded in every vector. Browser fields and expected wire bytes
are native inputs, never generated by the encoder under test. The four separate
peer capacities are 0, 128, 4096 and 65536. Native request stream IDs and per-section
acknowledgements are replayed explicitly; header sections and concatenated encoder
instructions must match in full.

The corpus establishes sequential codec behavior after SETTINGS with decoder
feedback before each next request. It does not establish initial connection
packet scheduling or arbitrary decoder-feedback races. The source report
explains independent semantic decoder gaps and the exact live comparison history:
https://github.com/enetx/surf/blob/v1.0.249/tests/testdata/wire/desktop_sequences/README.md

No runtime encoder or browser presets change in this release. Generic encoder
options remain caller-controlled; browser choices live in Surf profiles.
